solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Right in fashion and new?

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for right goes inside the fashion-plus-new letters

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or prevailing style

explanation.surface: A question about whether being on trend simply means being new.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes between the E and N of MODE + N. The whole clue doubles as the definition: something up to date is both stylish and new.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to date and novel: being stylish and recent is exactly what contemporary describes.

clue.text: Annual publication of long standing admits ruin, oddly

indicators.note: admits says the odd letters are let inside the magazine-plus-old letters

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of the word ruin

parts.note: something of long standing is old

explanation.surface: A yearly periodical with a long history lets in ruin, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annual' looks like a yearly publication, but it is the noun for a plant living one year.
explanation.definitionFit: A common garden flower grown from seed each year is a typical annual plant.

clue.text: I'd upset a judge? Could be grave

indicators.note: upset means the letters of I'd and a are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: a critic judges art or performances

explanation.surface: Someone worries that offending a judge could have grave consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' suggests seriousness but means the grave accent, a mark on a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave accent is one example of a mark added to a letter to change its sound.

clue.text: Educated woman introducing university lecturer's opening ceremony

indicators.note: introducing means the woman takes the university letter inside her

parts.note: Rita is the title character of the play and film Educating Rita

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of lecturer's

explanation.surface: A graduate woman brings in a university lecturer to open a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a British play and film by Willy Russell about a hairdresser studying with the Open University.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal set of solemn actions performed the same way each time is a ceremony.

clue.text: English town expels river vessel

indicators.note: expels says the town throws out the letter for river from its name

parts.note: Stockport is a town in Greater Manchester, England

explanation.surface: An English town banishes a boat from its river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River vessel' reads as one phrase, a riverboat, but 'river' belongs to the wordplay and 'vessel' alone is the definition, a cooking pot. Stockport is a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pot for simmering broth is a kitchen vessel, the container sense rather than a ship.

clue.text: Uttering it, ultimately we so will struggle?

definitions.text: Uttering it, ultimately we so will struggle?

indicators.note: will struggle says these letters wrestle themselves into a new order
ultimately keeps only the end of the word it, dropping its opening letter

explanation.surface: A warning that saying something will leave us all tongue-tied.
explanation.walkthrough: UTTERING, the T ending 'it' and WE SO are rearranged; 'will struggle' is the signal. The whole clue also defines: saying one, we will struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase designed to be hard to pronounce quickly makes any speaker stumble over the words.

clue.text: Fossilised resin is located under church hall

indicators.note: is located under places the resin below the church letters in this down entry

parts.note: amber is fossilised tree resin

explanation.surface: Some amber is found beneath a church hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church hall' reads as a phrase, but 'church' is CH and 'hall' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large room for meetings, as in a council chamber, is a hall.

clue.text: Animal defining the borders of Patagonia?

indicators.note: the borders of points to the outer letters of the region's name, which the answer describes when split into three words

parts.note: Patagonia is the southern region of Argentina and Chile; its first letter is P and its last is A

explanation.surface: A creature that marks the edges of a South American region.
explanation.walkthrough: Patagonia begins with P and ends with A; split into three words, the animal's name spells exactly that, and 'defining' links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-white bear from China is a well-known animal.

clue.text: One occupies business address that's heated

indicators.note: occupies means the numeral sits within the business word

parts.note: trade is business or commerce
one is I, as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: One person occupies a business premises that has central heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business address' looks like a location, but 'address' means a speech, and an angry one.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech is an address delivered in heat.

clue.text: Joint account centrally held by revolutionary despot

indicators.note: held by puts the central letter inside the turned-round ruler
revolutionary means the despot's title is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a tsar was an autocratic Russian ruler, a despot

indicators.note: centrally picks the central letter of the word account

explanation.surface: A shared bank account is seized by an overthrown tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint account' reads as one banking phrase, but 'Joint' alone is the definition. Turning TSAR round gives RAST, which holds O, the middle letter of 'account'.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of meat cooked in the oven is a roast, as in the Sunday roast.

clue.text: Can, say, criminal retain spoils?

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: spoils tells us the word retain is ruined and its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A question of whether a crook is allowed to keep his loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like the noun, loot, but it is the verb signalling a rearrangement of RETAIN into TAINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin can is an example of a receptacle, hence 'say' marking it as one instance.

clue.text: Country club possibly accepts one after vocal snub by representative

indicators.note: after places the club letters following the earlier pieces
vocal says the snub word is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: to check is to rebuff or rein in

indicators.note: accepts means the rearranged club takes in the letter for one
possibly says the letters of club may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A club admits a member after a snub from a representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' is the definition. UBLC (club rearranged) takes I to make UBLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A central European nation whose capital is Prague.

clue.text: European and oriental could be closely related

parts.note: a German is a European
E for East, so oriental gives E

explanation.surface: A remark that Europeans and Asians might be kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent or relevant: a point closely related to the matter in hand is apt to it.

clue.text: Revolting woven fabric for carpet

parts.note: a populace that is up is in revolt, so revolting gives UP
braid is woven or plaited fabric trim

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a disgusting rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like a floor covering, but here it is the verb, to reprimand, as when an employee is carpeted.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to haul them up and scold them, a British idiom for a telling-off.

clue.text: Fellow quits one instrument for another

indicators.note: quits says the fellow's letter leaves the first instrument

parts.note: a flute is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: A musician leaves one instrument and takes up a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'another' (instrument), and 'for' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked stringed instrument of the Renaissance, so a different instrument from the woodwind.

clue.text: Playing concerto's finale, Richter displays eloquence

indicators.note: Playing tells us the letters are performed in a new order
finale picks the closing letter of concerto

explanation.surface: A pianist named Richter performs a concerto's last movement with eloquence.
explanation.walkthrough: Sviatoslav Richter was a celebrated pianist, apt for the musical scene. O, the end of 'concerto's', joins RICHTER and the lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasive, fluent public speaking is the art of oratory, a near synonym for eloquence.

clue.text: She's a tart

definitions.meaning: a female name, so the clue words mean this woman is called by it
a fruit pudding baked in a mould lined with bread or sponge, akin to a tart

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a woman's morals.
explanation.walkthrough: The insult hides two meanings: a girl's name and a baked dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name shared with a fruit dessert baked in a bread-lined mould.

clue.text: Press statement suggesting Teddy's fallen?

definitions.meaning: to press down heavily, apply pressure
a teddy is a toy bear, so saying the toy is no longer upright describes it

explanation.surface: A news release hints that a toy bear has toppled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press statement' looks like a news release, but 'Press' is a verb and the rest a jokey second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert pressure downward is to press; the second reading has the toy lying flat.

clue.text: Eating place mostly edged by lake

indicators.note: mostly means the past-tense verb loses its last letter

parts.note: to edge is to move slowly, so edged gives crept
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A dining spot that is largely bordered by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edged' looks like 'bordered' but means crept; 'mostly' trims it to CREP.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant specialising in pancakes is a type of eating place.

clue.text: Green PE pants could be centrepiece for table

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, signalling the letters are made a mess of

explanation.surface: Green PE shorts could serve as a table decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers but is British slang for poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental stand of dishes for fruit or flowers placed in the middle of a dining table.

clue.text: Only some saw an evident decline

indicators.note: Only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only a few people witnessed an obvious downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle or diminish, as the moon does after full, is to decline.

clue.text: Secret police succeeded, making arrest

parts.note: the Stasi were the East German secret police
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Secret police make a successful arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' suggests a detention, but it means a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of standstill or halted flow, as in cardiac arrest.

clue.text: Setter's attitude is to take advantage

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, so setter's is I am, contracted
a pose is a bodily attitude or posture

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler's stance is to exploit people.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone's good nature, as in to presume on them.

clue.text: Expert stops Greek character making a scene

indicators.note: stops means the skilled word plugs the Greek letter like a stopper

parts.note: tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet
able means skilled, expert

explanation.surface: A skilled person blocks a Greek and causes a public fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a scene' suggests a commotion, but the definition is a scene in the theatrical sense, a frozen group.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking group of motionless figures, as on stage, is a picture or scene.

clue.text: Rising aristocrat penning lines as poet

indicators.note: Rising, in a down entry, means the combined letters read upwards
penning means the aristocrat encloses the railway letters

parts.note: a nob is a toff, an aristocrat
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: An upwardly mobile nobleman writing verses as a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet was himself a lord, so the aristocrat fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord George Gordon was a Romantic poet who wrote Don Juan.

clue.text: One walking unsteadily is denied second glass

indicators.note: is denied says the walker loses the letter for second

parts.note: a stumbler is someone who trips or walks unsteadily

explanation.surface: A tottering drunk is refused another glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a drinker being cut off, with 'second glass' meaning another drink; 'second' is S, and 'glass' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed drinking vessel without a stem is a common kind of glass.

clue.text: Lag, with rest beginning to gain ground? Taking run, he will!

definitions.text: Lag, with rest beginning to gain ground? Taking run, he will!

indicators.note: Taking says the rearranged letters then add the letter for run
ground, as in ground down, means these letters are crushed and remade
beginning to picks the opening letter of the word gain

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner falling behind wonders whether resting will help him catch up.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG + REST + G is rearranged to STRAGGLE, then R is added. The whole clue also defines: one who lags is the person who will lag.
explanation.definitionFit: A person trailing behind the group is one who lags, exactly what the clue's exclamation describes.

clue.text: Surpass United in no-score draw

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for United inside the two zeros

parts.note: a nil-nil draw is written 0-0, read as two letter Os
Utd is the usual abbreviation for United in football club names

explanation.surface: A football team's goalless draw, perhaps beating expectations.
explanation.walkthrough: Football scores are read as letters: 0-0 gives OO. Manchester United and others are shortened to Utd in British results tables.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to beat or exceed another's performance.

clue.text: One's lacking in awareness and judgment

indicators.note: lacking in says the numeral is missing from the awareness word

parts.note: sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, awareness
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: Someone without awareness or good judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judgment' looks like good sense, but it is a court's verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's judgment on a convicted criminal is the punishment it pronounces.

clue.text: Austrian composer or German one, note

parts.note: Carl Maria von Weber was a German composer

explanation.surface: A choice between an Austrian and a German composer, plus a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Anton Webern was an Austrian Second Viennese School composer; Weber was German.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Webern was a twentieth-century composer from Vienna, a pupil of Schoenberg.
